From: Tom Harper <tom.harper@medisys.com>

Cc: dpo@medisys.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Data routing & cross-border evidence — Medisys onboarding

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. We need to stitch together the documentation for our procurement and privacy teams. High level asks from med-legal / procurement:

- Confirmation of which contractual instruments Redwood will rely on for EU -> US processing (standard SCCs, UK IDTA/UK addendum, DTIAs/TIAs).
- Can Redwood provide a short plain‑language evidence pack (1–2 pages) that we can attach to our procurement packet describing routing, subprocessors, and KMS/key custody?
- For our regulated workloads we need to know whether customer‑managed KMS is available without key escrow, and the exact subprocessors list for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Required log retention windows (they asked for 13 months as a baseline).

Could you also include a fallback routing map (if capacity in eu-west is saturated, where will traffic fall back) and any timing estimates for producing a signed UK Addendum or SCCs? Procurement will need examples of the DPA redline and the TIA/DTIA language you typically accept.

We attached an evidence template they use (medisys-evidence-request.pdf).

Appreciate a short reply with bullets we can escalate internally — we’re trying to keep this at a 1–2 page summary.

Best,
Tom
Lead Security & Privacy — Medisys Health
[Attachment: medisys-evidence-request.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Tom Harper <tom.harper@medisys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data routing & cross-border evidence — Medisys onboarding

Tom — thanks for the clear ask and the template. I’ve outlined the short responses below and attached a 1‑page SCC/IDTA summary and a KMS keyflow diagram for the technical reviewers. More detail follows afterwards.

Quick bullets you can pass to procurement / privacy (1 page):
- Contractual instruments: Redwood supports EU Standard Contractual Clauses (legal basis for transfers) and will execute the UK IDTA/UK addendum when requested. We typically propose SCCs by default; UK Addendum is available as an executed addendum for UK personal data.
- TIAs/DTIAs: We provide Transfer Impact Assessments on request for high‑risk geographies. For Medisys, we can produce a scoped TIA for EU -> US transfers (2–3 week turnaround) and include our technical mitigations and routing attestations.
- KMS/key custody: Private deployments and VPC private packages support customer‑managed keys (BYOK) with no Redwood key escrow. For Hosted plans, we offer managed KMS with optional HSM-backed keys; escrow is NOT the default but can be discussed in an enterprisey SOW.
- Subprocessors: current list for Dedicated/Private attached (subprocessors-current.csv). For Hosted, subprocessors differ slightly — we’ll surface a per‑environment split if you need it.
- Logs: default observability retention is 6 months; we can extend to 13 months under an enterprise retention addendum for Dedicated/Private.
- Fallback routing: primary: eu‑west (Frankfurt), fallback: eu‑central (Netherlands), then us‑east for non‑sensitive workloads. Private deployments can be pinned to EU only.

Attachments: redwood-scc-summary.pdf (1p), kms-keyflow-diagram.png, subprocessors-current.csv.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Legal: Marissa / Rishi will propose DPA redline and confirm UK IDTA signature cadence (Marissa).
2) Security: I’ll schedule a short call to walk through the KMS keyflow and the scoped TIA requirements (30 min).
3) Procurement: if you can confirm PO cadence and whether your procurement requires an executed UKAddendum or SCC signature first, we’ll prioritize that doc.

If that looks good I’ll circulate a 1‑page PDF for your packet by end of day.

—Kimberly
Director, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-scc-summary.pdf (PDF, 210KB)]

Appreciate it.
Tom

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Tom — quick legal clarification on the two items you flagged:

1) TIA attestation vs DTIA annex: Redwood can provide a signed Transfer Impact Attestation for vendor‑hosted services covering technical and organisational safeguards, routing assertions, and subprocessors. For healthcare workloads where customers require contractually binding DTIA language, we do offer a DTIA annex but it typically requires a short legal review and signature (timeline 2–3 weeks once scope is finalized). For most pilot/proof‑of‑concepts the attestation suffices; for production commitments we recommend the DTIA annex.

2) BYOK wording for procurement: you may use the following sentence in your SOW / PO: "Redwood will support customer-managed keys for Private deployments; customer is solely responsible for key custody and Redwood will not retain or escrow customer key material unless separately agreed in writing." If you need HSM import specifics (PKCS#11 / Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS), we can add an integration note.

On logging/retention: the cost delta depends on throughput and whether data is stored in cold tier. For a 13‑month retention addendum on Dedicated, our preliminary estimate is +8–12% on observability costs (we’ll route to Finance for a firm number).

I’ve recorded this in HubSpot under the deal and linked to the compliance packet here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-4391 (internal view).

If Medisys needs the DTIA annex redline, Marissa can start that and we’ll include the UK Addendum signature option.

—Rishi
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference
